`analyzeLandscape` now works as a second name for `updateLandscape`, but I could not run it. Compilation passes, and the `cli` module has no tests. Running the built jar and `git diff` both hit a permission prompt I didn't get approved, so the behaviour is verified by reading the code only.

What changed:

- **`cli/.../Commands.java`**: added `ANALYZE_LANDSCAPE = "analyzeLandscape"` with a description calling it the landscape counterpart of the analysis commands, same as `updateLandscape`. It is listed in the no-argument usage overview right after `updateLandscape`, using the same options.
- **`cli/.../CommandLineInterface.java`**: both names dispatch to `updateLandscape`, which now takes the command name and description as parameters. `-help` therefore prints the usage for whichever name was typed, and the behaviour and options are identical.
- **`README.md`**: the README had no command reference, so there was nothing to update. I added a short "Landscape report" section describing both commands.

I also ran `mvn -o -pl cli package -DskipTests`, which left build output in `cli/target`. Nothing was committed.

To check it, run `java -jar cli/target/cli-1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar analyzeLandscape -help` and `analyzeLandscape -analysisRoot <folder>` against a folder.
